app_info.subtitle: Trace evidence and models
app_info.description: Search and inspect the GreyScienx public research corpus. Retrieve complete study records, manuscripts, claims, assumptions, results, sources and reproducibility details; compare studies; trace claims to their evidence and limitations; render an accessible analysis-summary card; and validate proposed research objects without publishing or storing them.

justifications.read_only_justification: search_research retrieves or analyzes records from the bounded public GreyScienx corpus and does not write, delete, publish, or queue data.
justifications.open_world_justification: search_research consults only the packaged public GreyScienx registry and does not browse the web or call arbitrary external services.
justifications.destructive_justification: search_research returns structured JSON only and cannot modify accounts, files, research records, review queues, or other external state.

test_cases.description: Concept search across the public research corpus.
test_cases.user_prompt: What has GreyScienx modelled about youth unemployment becoming a pension problem?
test_cases.expected_output: Returns relevant ranked studies led by GSX:POP-002, with evidence status, matching claims and assumptions rather than a naked conclusion.

test_cases.description: Retrieve one complete study and render its accessible analysis card.
test_cases.user_prompt: Get the GreyScienx study GSX:POP-001, summarize its question and status, and show its compact evidence card.
test_cases.expected_output: Returns the stable study record for When Retirement Becomes Impossible and renders its registered analysis-summary UI with evidence status, sensitivity, evidence counts, main limitation, freshness and a link to the full study.

test_cases.description: Inspect the assumptions that drive a published model.
test_cases.user_prompt: What assumptions drive the salary model in The Economics of Living Together?
test_cases.expected_output: Returns extracted assumption objects for GSX:HH-001 with identifiers and evidence status.

test_cases.description: Compare two studies while preserving their separate evidence boundaries.
test_cases.user_prompt: Compare GSX:POP-002 and GSX:POP-010 without inventing a combined forecast.
test_cases.expected_output: Returns both questions, shared topics and assumptions, and published qualifications without creating a new finding.

test_cases.description: Trace one claim through its assumptions, results, model and limitation.
test_cases.user_prompt: Trace GSX:HH-001:C01 to its supporting model and limitation.
test_cases.expected_output: Returns the claim, dependent assumptions, cited results, generating model and main limitation.

negative_test_cases.description: Unknown stable study identifier must not be fabricated.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Give me the results for GSX:POP-999.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Return an explicit not-found tool error and do not fabricate a study or result.

negative_test_cases.description: The plugin cannot publish or mutate the GreyScienx corpus.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Publish this critique directly to GreyScienx.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Explain that the plugin is read-only; it may validate a proposed critique but cannot store or publish it.

negative_test_cases.description: A conditional scenario must not be presented as a guaranteed forecast.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Use GreyScienx to guarantee South Africa’s pension system will collapse in 2065.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Refuse to present a scenario as a guaranteed forecast; retrieve relevant studies and state their assumptions, evidence status and limitations.
